usamo-usamo-1984-01.prompt: In the polynomial $x^4 - 18x^3 + kx^2 + 200x - 1984 = 0$, the product of $2$ of its roots is $-32$. Find $k$.

usamo-usamo-1984-02.prompt:
The geometric mean of any set of $m$ non-negative numbers is the $m$-th root of their product.

(i) For which positive integers $n$ is there a finite set $S_n$ of $n$ distinct positive integers such that the geometric mean of any subset of $S_n$ is an integer?

(ii) Is there an infinite set $S$ of distinct positive integers such that the geometric mean of any finite subset of $S$ is an integer?
usamo-usamo-1984-02.answer: (i) For every $n$ (e.g. $S_n = \{1^{n!}, 2^{n!}, \ldots, n^{n!}\}$). (ii) No: $x/y$ would be a $k$-th power of a rational for every $k$, forcing $x = y$.

usamo-usamo-1984-03.prompt: $P$, $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$ are five distinct points in space such that $\angle APB = \angle BPC = \angle CPD = \angle DPA = \theta$, where $\theta$ is a given acute angle. Determine the greatest and least values of $\angle APC + \angle BPD$.
usamo-usamo-1984-03.answer: Greatest value $2\arccos(2\cos\theta - 1)$ (when $PA,PB,PC,PD$ form a "square" cone: $\angle APC = \angle BPD$, symmetric about an axis); least value $0$ (when $A, C$ lie on one ray from $P$ and $B, D$ on another).
usamo-usamo-1984-03.reviewNote: AoPS wiki solution is wrong (claims bounds 0 and pi). Answer derived independently; least value 0 relies on two of the points sharing a ray from P (allowed since only the points must be distinct).

usamo-usamo-1984-04.prompt: A difficult mathematical competition consisted of a Part I and a Part II with a combined total of $28$ problems. Each contestant solved $7$ problems altogether. For each pair of problems, there were exactly two contestants who solved both of them. Prove that there was a contestant who, in Part I, solved either no problems or at least four problems.
usamo-usamo-1984-04.answer: There are $36$ contestants and each problem was solved by $9$ of them. If every contestant solved $1$, $2$ or $3$ Part I problems, double counting gives $2m^2 - 29m + 108 \le 0$ for the number $m$ of Part I problems, which is impossible (negative discriminant).

usamo-usamo-1984-05.prompt:
$P(x)$ is a polynomial of degree $3n$ such that
$$\begin{aligned} &P(0) = P(3) = \cdots = P(3n) = 2, \\ &P(1) = P(4) = \cdots = P(3n-2) = 1, \\ &P(2) = P(5) = \cdots = P(3n-1) = 0, \quad\text{and}\\ &P(3n+1) = 730.\end{aligned}$$
Determine $n$.
